([[Hyattsville, Maryland]]) | college = [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] (2010–2013) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | career_end = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *[[Sporting News|TSN]] National Player of the Year (2013) * Co-[[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] (2013) * First Team Consensus All-American ([[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2013]]) * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Defensive Player of the Year ([[2012–13 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2013]]) * 1st Team All-Big Ten (2013) | stat1label = | stat1value = | stat2label = | stat2value = | stat3label = | stat3value = | letter = | bbr = | HOF_player = | FIBA_HOF_player = }} '''Victor Oladipo''' (born May 4, 1992) is a junior [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball]] team at [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University]]. His combination of explosive athleticism, fearless defense, and efficient shooting has drawn comparisons to [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Michael Jordan]].{{cite web | url=http://www.thebiglead.com/index.php/2013/02/02/victor-oladipo-dunked-and-dick-vitale-lost-his-mind/ | title=Victor Oladipo Dunked, and Dick Vitale Lost His Mind | publisher=ESPN | accessdate=February 3, 2013}} In 2013, he was named the [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' Men's College Basketball Player of the Year]], the [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year|National Co-Defensive Player of the Year]], and a First Team [[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2013 All-American]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] and ''[[Sporting News]]''. ==Early life and high school== Oladipo is the son of [[Nigeria|Nigerian]] mother Joan Amanze and [[Sierra Leone|Sierra Leonean]] father Christopher, who immigrated to the US in the 1985. Joan is a nurse and Christopher has a PHD in [[behavioral science]] from [[University of Maryland, College Park]] {{cite web|last=Layden|first=Tim|title=Victor Oladipo's rise from overlooked recruit to Indiana superstar|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/-college-basketball-mens-tournament/news/20130319/victor-oladipo/|work=Sports Illustrated|accessdate=June 24, 2013|date=March 25, 2013}}. He is the only son; he has sisters Kristine(1986), Kendra(1990)http://www.thebuffandblue.net/?p=11142 ''The Oladipo Factor'', and twin sister Victoria http://www.indystar.com/article/20130109/SPORTS0601/301090339/Indiana-basketball-women-Victor-Oladipo-s-family-keep-him-grounded The women in Victor Oladipo's family keep him grounded. His sister Kendra is [[deaf]] http://www.gallaudetathletics.com/news/2012-13/indianapractice . Oladipo played high school basketball at [[DeMatha High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]]{{cite web|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/04/14/AR2010041404565.html|title=Victor Oladipo has had an incredible career; he just wishes his father would have seen it|author=Barr, Josh|publisher=Washington Post|date=April 15, 2010|accessdate=February 2, 2013}} . As a senior he averaged 11.9 points, 10.3 rebounds and 3.6 blocks per game. He led DeMatha to a 32-4 record and the [[Washington Catholic Athletic Conference]] and City championships. Oladipo was named to the Washington Post 2010 All-Met First Team and the First Team All-WCAC. He was ranked No. 144 overall and the No. 41 shooting guard in his class by [[Rivals.com]]. [[Scout.com]] listed him as the No. 39 shooting guard in his class and [[ESPN]] put him at No. 53 at his position.{{cite web|title=Victor Oladipo Profile|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/oladipo_victor00.html|publisher=Indiana University Athletic Department|accessdate=7 April 2012}} ==College career== Oladipo chose to play basketball for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana University]] and major in sports communication broadcast, turning down offers from [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].{{cite web|title=Victor Oladipo|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Victor-Oladipo-84192|publisher=Rivals.com|accessdate=7 April 2012}} Upon his commitment to Indiana he said, "It's like a basketball atmosphere everywhere you go....It's a basketball town. That's perfect."{{cite news|last=Bozich|first=Alex|title=Victor Oladipo joins Indiana’s 2010 class|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2009/09/07/victor-oladipo-joins-indianas-2010-class/|accessdate=7 April 2012|newspaper=Inside the Hall|date=7 September 2009}} ===Freshman season=== As a freshman during the [[2010–11 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2010-11 season]], Oladipo played in 32 games and started five. He earned his first career start that year against [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]] and scored 14 points on 5-of-9 shooting, four rebounds, three steals and two assists in 27 minutes of action. He made his second career start against No. 2 The Ohio State and responded with 14 points and six rebounds. ===Sophomore season=== [[File:20120105 Tim Hardaway Jr vs Victor Oladipo.jpg |thumb|left|Oladipo defends against [[Tim Hardaway, Jr.]] on January 5, 2012.]] As a sophomore during the [[2011–12 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2011-12 season]] Oladipo averaged 10.9 points and 5.5 rebounds in 26.7 minutes per game (47.1% FG, 75% FT). Some commentators referred to him as Indiana's "most improved player this season" and he was often cited as the team's best defender.{{cite news|last=Albers|first=Justin|title=That's a Wrap: Victor Oladipo|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2012/04/05/thats-a-wrap-victor-oladipo-2/|accessdate=7 April 2012|newspaper=Inside the Hall|date=5 April 2012}} Oladipo scored 10 or more points in 21 games in the season, 11 more games than the previous year. He also increased his free-throw percentage from 61 to 75, and he got there four times per game. The Hoosiers' record in [[2011–12 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2011-2012]] improved by fifteen games over the prior season, making it the largest single turnaround in the NCAA that year. The team earned a number four seed in the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA Tournament]] and defeated [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] in the second round. After defeating [[Virginia Commonwealth University Rams men's basketball|VCU]] in the third round, the Hoosiers lost in the Sweet Sixteen to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], the eventual national champions. ===Junior season=== As a junior during the [[2012–13 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2012-13 season]] Oladipo emerged as one of the team's principal stars. Despite a roster deep with talent, including Preseason Player of the Year [[Cody Zeller]], Oladipo emerged as one of the nation's biggest stars.{{cite news | url=http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/71398/oladipo-emerges-as-hoosiers-star | title=Oladipo emerges as Hoosiers' star | date=December 31, 2012 | accessdate=January 1, 2013 | author=Brennan, Eamonn}} Midway through the season [[ESPN]] writer Eamonn Brenann wrote, "In 2½ seasons in Bloomington, Oladipo has morphed from a raw athletic specimen to a defensive specialist/energy glue guy -- he became a hit with IU fans for holding his hand in front of his face after dunks at home, typically after a steal he himself created -- into a sudden, stunning, bona fide collegiate star." Due in part to Oladipo's leadership, the Indiana Hoosiers finished the 2012-13 season as the outright Big Ten champions. At the end of the regular season Oladipo ranked fourth in the country in field-goal percentage (61.4), on pace to have the highest field-goal percentage by any guard since the 1996-97 season.{{cite web | url=http://www.espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/79138/why-oladipo-should-win-wooden-award | title=Why Oladipo should win Wooden Award | publisher=ESPN | date=March 13, 2013 | accessdate=March 13, 2013 | author=Feldman, Ryan}} He ranked third in the nation in true shooting percentage (68.4), which measures shooting efficiency that takes into account field goals, 3-point field goals and free throws. And he averaged 1.39 points per play and shot 73.9% on offensive rebound put-backs, both of which ranked among the top five in the country. On defense Oladipo was arguably even more dominating. In a game [[2012–13 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|that season]] against #1 Michigan, he guarded four different players in 45 possessions, but only gave up 4 points.{{cite web | url=https://twitter.com/JayBilas/status/297939527652216832 | title=Jay Bilas on Twitter | accessdate=February 3, 2013 | author=Bilas, Jay}} Among Wooden Award finalists, he had the best net rating—which is the difference between points produced and points allowed per 100 possessions. Oladipo produces 42 more points than he allowed per 100 possessions. Each game he drew the opponent's top perimeter player, and his 5 percent steal rate (2.2 per game) ranked 15th in the country. His 69 steals in the season is second all-time at Indiana to [[Isiah Thomas]] who had 74 during the 1980-81 national championship season. He averaged 13.7 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 2.2 steals per game.{{cite web | url=http://indiana.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1482278 | title=Oladipo, Zeller head IU Big 10 honorees | publisher=Rivals.com | accessdate=March 12, 2013 | author=Rabjohns, Jeff}} He was also one of only two players from major conferences averaging at least 13 points, 6 rebounds, 2 assists and 2 steals per game this season. At the conclusion of his junior year Oladipo racked up numerous awards. He was named the [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' Men's College Basketball Player of the Year]], the [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year|National Co-Defensive Player of the Year]], and a First Team [[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2013 All-American]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] and ''[[Sporting News]]''. In conference honors he was named a unanimous pick to the First Team All-Big Ten by both the coaches and media, and was named Big Ten Defensive Player of the year. ==Professional career== ===2013 NBA Draft=== On April 9th 2013 at a press conference with Tom Crean, Oladipo announced that he was forgoing his senior season at Indiana and entering the [[2013 NBA Draft]]. He is projected to be a lottery pick by ESPN and CBS Sports. Victor Oladipo was invited to sit in the "green room" during the draft ==Player profile== Oladipo is a [[shooting guard]] who is also capable of playing [[small forward]]. Indiana coach [[Tom Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]] would frequently attribute Oladipo's success to his extreme work ethic and pre-game preparation of reviewing film. Oladipo is known for entertaining fans with exciting dunks. As announcer [[Clark Kellogg]] noted, "Victor Oladipo is like a baby's bottom, smooth and sometimes... explosive."{{cite web | url=http://network.yardbarker.com/college_basketball/article_external/clark_kellogg_compares_victor_oladipo_to_a/12885628/ | title=Announcer's odd comparison for Oladipo | publisher=Yard Barker | accessdate=February 10, 2013}} On offense, Oladipo is capable of aggressively and quickly [[Penetration (basketball)|driving]] to the basket, aided by unparalleled athletic leaping ability. Following a victory by Indiana over #1 ranked Michigan, coach [[John Beilein]] remarked, "I've seen a lot of players. I don't know whether I've seen one quicker or faster, more athletic, than Oladipo. It's tough to stay in front of him."{{cite web | url=http://sports.yahoo.com/news/ncaab--indiana-beats-michigan--no--1-ranking-awaits-college-basketball-s-most-entertaining-team-070029295.html | title=Indiana beats Michigan; No. 1 ranking awaits college basketball's most entertaining team | publisher=Yahoo! | accessdate=February 3, 2013 | author=Forde, Pat}} His offensive proficiency improved as his outside shooting range improved each year of his collegiate career. On defense, Oladipo is a "lockdown off-ball defender who can defend multiple positions".{{cite web | url=http://insider.espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/ncbexperts/id/8916720/michigan-trey-burke-top-10-closers-country-college-basketball | title=Top 10 closers in college hoops | publisher=ESPN.com | date=February 5, 2013 | accessdate=February 5, 2013 | author=Greenberg, Seth}} He has the quickness to guard point guards and the strength and athleticism to fight around a forward and get to a front if caught in a mismatch. His athleticism and anticipation makes it hard to set a screen on him.
